clue.text: When darkening skies are tinged with gilt anew?

definitions.text: When darkening skies are tinged with gilt anew?

indicators.note: anew means made over again, so the letters of these two words are formed afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A poetic question about the time of evening when the sky turns golden again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anew' rearranges WITH and GILT; the whole clue also describes the time of day, when the sky darkens and is touched with gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The half-light after sunset, when the sky darkens and often glows golden, is that period of dusk.

parts.note: not the front of a motor-racing grid but a place at or near the North Pole

explanation.surface: A motor-racing term asking about the front spot on the starting grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying within the polar circle in the far north is literally a position at the Pole.

clue.text: To get a drink change a quid, one the Revenue returned

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters in the two words beside it

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: returned means the abbreviation is written backwards

parts.note: IR stands for Inland Revenue, the former British tax authority

explanation.surface: Someone breaks a pound note to buy a drink after the taxman sent back their money.
explanation.walkthrough: A quid is British slang for a pound. 'change' rearranges A QUID into DAIQU; 'returned' turns IR (Inland Revenue) into RI.
explanation.definitionFit: A rum cocktail with lime juice and sugar is a well-known mixed drink.

parts.note: S is the compass direction south
a sign is something that indicates or points the way

explanation.surface: A road signpost gets given a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: To award something to someone is to allot or allocate it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Warning a worker is about to fight

indicators.note: is about means the first word goes around the second, enclosing it

parts.note: a worker bee is the classic crossword worker
war is armed fighting

explanation.surface: An alert that a labourer is on the point of starting a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is itself a cautionary command, so it serves as a warning.

clue.text: Serve one's sweetheart extremely nice wine

parts.note: a beau is a boyfriend or admirer

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme letters, the first and last, of the following word

explanation.surface: Advice to pour your lover a really lovely glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serve' is a link joining the instruction to the wine; 'extremely' takes N and E, the first and last letters of 'nice'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaune is a red Burgundy, named after the town in the Côte d'Or that produces it.

parts.note: a pass is success in an exam
up means at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: A student passing exams while at college.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you are 'up' at university while studying there.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline or let an opportunity go by is to ignore it, a phrasal-verb synonym.

indicators.note: End exited says the final letter has left the word before it

parts.note: taken as written, the Lancashire town

explanation.surface: Football fans leave Preston North End's ground in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: Preston North End is an English football club. N (North), the end letter of PRESTON, leaves it.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the Italian tempo direction presto means very fast, hence rapidly.

clue.text: Chess expert makes a terrific teacher

parts.note: grand means excellent or terrific
a schoolmaster is a teacher

explanation.surface: A chess champion turns out to be an excellent tutor.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandmaster is the highest title awarded to a chess player, so a chess expert.

clue.text: Prescription for sober man with a healthy heart

indicators.note: heart says the second piece sits at the centre of the first

parts.note: TT means teetotal, a person who does not drink
able means fit and able-bodied

explanation.surface: Advice for a non-drinker in good cardiac health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prescription' suggests a medical note, but here it means something prescribed; 'with a' is only a link, and TT is the crossword shorthand for teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pill is something a doctor prescribes, so a tablet can stand for a prescription.

clue.text: Paid back though completely in debt

indicators.note: in places the word for completely within the word for debt

parts.note: in the red means in debt
quite means completely, as in 'quite right'

explanation.surface: Money was returned even though the borrower was utterly broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Requited love or a requited favour is one returned in kind, so paid back.

indicators.note: to means the horse is attached to the pole, placed beside it

parts.note: S is south pole
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: Tethering a horse to a post.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is an unexpected problem, the same as a hitch.

clue.text: Service chief joins Tina in trip round US city

parts.note: C-in-C is commander-in-chief, the head of an armed service

indicators.note: trip round suggests tumbling and turning, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A military commander joins a woman on a tour of an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: C-in-C is a standard military abbreviation; 'trip round' signals an anagram, and the shuffled letters make up the second half of the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cincinnati is a city in Ohio in the United States.

indicators.note: potential means what the letters could become when rearranged

explanation.surface: Railway safety rules made simpler to cope with possible train crashes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'procedures for' is a link reading; 'potential' rearranges DERAILMENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Made more efficient by removing unnecessary steps, as streamlined processes are, so simplified.

parts.note: dispiriting not as depressing but as driving spirits out of a possessed person

explanation.surface: A man whose job is depressing.
explanation.definitionFit: One who casts out demons from a possessed person literally removes spirits for a living.

clue.text: Bury the hatchet, though put in jeopardy?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, finish one's fury
to expose to danger or risk

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition splits the answer as END ANGER, which is what burying the hatchet does.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone in jeopardy is to place them at risk, the plain verb sense.

parts.note: not a collector of trophies but someone always seeking pot, slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A sportsman chasing trophies.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dependent on a drug, always seeking more, is an addict.

definitions.meaning: the foot of something is its lowest part

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the buttocks and the lowest point of something, like the foot of a page.

parts.note: a paradox: something called lazy that keeps people's tongues working hard

explanation.surface: An exclamation that something keeps people talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointless chatter about others is inactive in purpose yet keeps people talking.

parts.note: not a window shutter but the fold of skin that shuts over the eye while we sleep

explanation.surface: A window shutter kept shut after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin fold that closes over the eye during sleep is a natural shutter.

parts.note: not a parliamentary bill but the Old Bill, British slang for the officers who keep law and order

explanation.surface: A piece of legislation intended to maintain public order.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Bill is British slang for the police force.
explanation.definitionFit: The force that keeps public order is called the Old Bill in British slang.

clue.text: An opening celebration or its finale

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
taken as written

explanation.surface: A party at which a door marks both the arrival and the farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its finale' adds a picture: a party ends when guests are shown the way out.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorway is an opening in a wall through which people pass.

clue.text: A know-all appears perceptive with port

parts.note: wise means shrewd or perceptive
Acre is a port in northern Israel

explanation.surface: A smart alec looks clever with a glass of port.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is someone who pretends to know everything, a know-all.

clue.text: A good one is important to one bowling from end to end

definitions.text: A good one is important to one bowling
definitions.meaning: a cricket bowler must pitch the ball at a good distance down the pitch
the measurement of something from one end to the other

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler aims to pitch the ball the right distance short of the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: The distance from one end of an object to the other is its long measurement.

indicators.note: new says the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Wanting a new piece of casual clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong craving for something is a thirst, as in a thirst for knowledge.

definitions.meaning: something hilarious is said to be a riot

explanation.definitionFit: A loud cry shows fear, and an amusing thing is informally called hilarious, the idiom 'it's a ...'.
